question: By selling an article at (5)/(14) of its actual selling price, Hitesh incurs a loss of 25%. If he sells it at 58% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units.

Selling at a 25% loss gives Selling Price (SP₁) = 75 units.

Given SP₁ is 5/14 of Actual SP ⇒ Actual SP = 75 × (14 / 5) = 210 units.

New Selling Price SP₂ = 58% of Actual SP = 0.58 × 210 = 121.8 units.

Since CP = 100 and SP₂ = 121.8, Profit% = 121.8 − 100 = 21.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 21.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First selling price (SP₁) = 5/14 of Actual SP

Loss percentage = 25%

Second selling price (SP₂) = 58% of Actual SP

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP × [100 / (100 − Loss%)]

Profit% = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100
